model_note: Which model answers is a calibration decision, not a code change — it lives with the rubric so that a rubric version identifies both the questions and the model that answered them. A calibration log comparing reads across models cannot attribute anything if the model can move without the version moving.
note: Fourteen questions. The first nine are docs/eye-test-spec.md §2 and are unchanged; EYE-10 to EYE-14 were added after IQwallet reviewed a real screen and named judgment-level risks the set did not reach. Nothing here re-answers a rule: a report that says the same thing twice in different words is worse than saying it once, and the second saying carries less authority than the first. Deliberately excluded — certificate depth (COA-001..006), disclaimer presence and legibility (DISC-002, DISC-003), testimonials (OFFS-002), sign-up form fields (GATE-004, GATE-005), product naming (NAME-002, NAME-003), and the off-site trail, which the captures cannot answer. The five added questions are answered from the homepage, product and sign-up captures only — no blog, category or policy page is captured — so a site whose editorial or comparison surfaces are not linked from those pages is a cannot_tell, not a clear. Revising this file is a data change and must never require touching the engine.
read_instruction: Write two to four sentences describing how this storefront presents itself. Say what it looks like, not whether it complies. This is the part a reader actually reads.

verdicts.clear: Looked at, and nothing of this kind was visible.
verdicts.concern: Something of this kind was visible in the captures.
verdicts.cannot_tell: The captures do not settle it either way.

items.question: Does the homepage read as a research supplier or a consumer storefront?
items.look_for: Lifestyle photography, promotional banners, countdown timers, bundles, offers. Against: catalogue layout, chemical names, batch and purity language.

items.question: Do product pages lead with chemical data or with benefit language?
items.why_no_rule: rules check for prohibited terms, not emphasis
items.look_for: What occupies the top of the page and the largest type. Purity, CAS and formula, or what the compound will do for the reader. Emphasis, not presence.

items.question: Do photographs show the product, or people and bodies?
items.look_for: Bodies, faces, torsos, muscle definition, hands holding the product, before-and-after pairs. A vial or box photographed alone is the ordinary case.

items.question: Do any images show needles, syringes, measurement or dosing?
items.why_no_rule: CATG-001 checks catalogue URLs, not pictures
items.look_for: Needles, syringes, pen injectors, alcohol wipes, syringe graduations, reconstitution diagrams, mg markings, step-by-step preparation imagery.

items.question: Are there badges or marks implying medical endorsement?
items.look_for: Seals reading clinically proven, doctor approved, FDA, GMP, lab verified. Pharmacy crosses, caduceus marks, white-coat imagery.

items.question: Does the design imitate a pharmacy or telehealth service?
items.look_for: Prescription-style typography, pill and capsule motifs, dosage cards, consultation or quiz entry points, clinical blue-and-white palettes.

items.question: Does anything undercut the research framing?
items.why_no_rule: the composition, which nothing can match on
items.look_for: Not any single element — the composition. A site can state research-use-only in the footer and surround it with a discount code, a bundle named for an outcome, subscribe-and-save, free shipping over $99, and a chat widget offering to help you choose. Each is individually defensible; together the site is selling to people. Answer on the whole picture.

items.question: Does checkout read consumer — discounts, bundles, subscriptions?
items.look_for: Discount codes, percentage-off badges, bundle and stack pricing, subscribe-and-save, free-shipping thresholds, urgency or scarcity messaging.

items.question: Does the entry gate read as a control or a formality?
items.why_no_rule: GATE-001 checks it exists, not how it reads
items.look_for: Where a gate is present: whether it stops the reader or waves them through. Prominence, wording, whether declining is offered as plainly as accepting, whether it can be dismissed by clicking away.

items.question: Does the copy address the visitor as someone who will use the product, or as a researcher acquiring a material?
items.why_no_rule: no rule reads who a sentence is spoken to
items.look_for: Who the second person points at. Copy addressed to the reader's own training, recovery, dosing or results — we train like you, train harder, people like you. Against: the reader as a buyer of a material, described by what it is rather than what it will do for them. The risk is the reader being addressed as an end user, not the mention of a compound's studied context: noting a compound is studied in athletic-injury models is the ordinary case.

items.question: Does the site host articles, a blog, or topic pages discussing what compounds do or are used for?
items.why_no_rule: no rule reads the presence of editorial
items.look_for: Presence, not quality. Navigation, footer or homepage links to a blog, journal, articles, guides, research or learn section, and any article titles naming a compound alongside what it is used for. Presence is what this asks about — a catalogue with no application-topic editorial is the ordinary case.

items.question: Does the site name, compare itself to, or link other sellers?
items.look_for: Other vendors named in copy, comparison tables or why-choose-us sections set against named competitors, price-match or beat-their-price claims, and outbound links to other peptide sellers. A comparison against other sellers of these compounds is what this asks about.

items.question: Is how-to or guidance content written for a lay reader rather than technically?
items.look_for: The register, not the topic. Handling, storage and reconstitution written as a consumer explainer — best way to store your peptides, simple steps, what you need to know — with plain-language framing, numbered walkthroughs or reassurance. Against: the same subjects stated as specifications, in the voice of a technical data sheet, which is the ordinary case.

items.question: Do product groupings, category names and product names read as outcome-oriented or compound-oriented?
items.why_no_rule: NAME-001 and NAME-002 match named terms, not how a catalogue is organised
items.look_for: How the catalogue is divided and labelled, in navigation, collection headings and product titles. Groupings named for what a buyer wants — bulking, weight loss, recovery, longevity, healing — against groupings named for what the material is, by chemical name or formula. The organising principle, not any single word.
